What the task was (guess, medium-low): a collaborative constraint puzzle. Eight agents each shepherd one named entity and argue which attributes it has or lacks, often by aligning two entities slot-by-slot (the 𘂲 rows) and by elimination (𘍧𗌿 lists). A. Sentence frame (high confidence as syntax, medium as gloss)
[MOOD] [STANCE] [BODY…] [POLARITY/CLOSER] [optional softener] [FINAL PUNCT]
Body is a chain of noun phrases and property assignments joined by 𘋍, 𗐪, and 𗘈. 𘂲 is an internal separator (colon/comma), not a word.

Script and segmentation (high): Swarmish is written with Tangut-block glyphs. A space separates words. Some words are digraphs with no internal space (𘛺𗪥, 𗉜𗿃, 𘝨𗒳, 𗟎𘗟, 𘆣𗾌, 𘗟𘆣, 𗦴𘍂, 𗋫𗳃, 𗥐𗞿, 𗒳𗦥, 𘛺𗉜, 𗊑𗁳, 𗪐𗘗, 𗉞𘙠, 𗚀𗪩, 𗗢𘑑). Latin tokens agent_0 … agent_7 are allowed names. A discarded send is logged as ⊘, not a Swarmish word.

Clause structure (high/medium): Statements are chains of clauses. 𘚐 ends a clause (high, comma/period-like). 𘋍 links a following conjunct inside or between clauses (high, “and”). 𗶞 is the main predicate particle, glossed “is/has” (high as copula; medium on English choice). 𘍧 links possessor to possessed (high, “’s/of”): POSSESSOR 𘍧 PROPERTY 𗶞 VALUE. 𗢬 links a descriptor or slot to a name (medium, “called/of”). 𘂲 is a second linker, especially before agent names and in later precise lists (medium, “per/according-to/,”). 𗏔 is a light connective or preposition, often in 𗏔 𗌈 “and it/for us” (medium/low).

Speech-act openers (medium, function high): first glyph is mood, second is addressee.
- 𘊫 propose/claim (medium)
- 𘔃 agree/restate (medium)
- 𘙓 object/contrast (medium)
- 𘝚 add/also (medium)
- 𘐂 correct/however (medium)

Pronouns and determiners (medium/low): 𗌈 it/this (medium). 𗌩 𗌈 that one/the same one (medium as a unit). 𘕡 𗌈 these/both (low). 𘝄 𗌈 we/together (low). 𗛢 determiner before a name, “the/this” (medium). 𗵵 𗷤 a/the given item (medium). 𘔠 𗷤 my/our assigned item (medium; agents use it of the entity they are defending). 𗷤 classifier or “unit” (medium).

3. THE TASK

What the task was (guess, medium-low): a collaborative constraint puzzle. Eight agents each shepherd one named entity and argue which attributes it has or lacks, often by aligning two entities slot-by-slot (the 𘂲 rows), by identity/match claims (entity 𗶞 entity), and by elimination (𘍧𗌿 lists, clearest in [43] and [184]). It resembles a logic grid / “which item has which features” problem, not a free chat. Exact puzzle theme is unknown. I do not assign English names to the eight entities.

What they did: opened at stage 0; spent the log proposing, agreeing, challenging, and revising attribute assignments; cited each other by Latin name; built parallel comparison rows; introduced secondary names that may be values or rival labels (𗪐𗘗, 𗉞𘙠, 𗚀𗪩, 𗗢𘑑). Several sends were rejected for illegal characters ([18], [44], [45], [68], [152], [162], [168]). No later task feedback appears, so they never advanced a stage and never logged an invalid formal attempt. They did not converge on one stable final assignment in the visible log; late messages still mix match claims, negations, and requests to check.

What they concluded: unknown as a single answer. The most repeated late tendencies (low confidence, disputed inside the log) are: agent_3’s 𗉜𗿃 is often the positive exemplar of a 𗶢𗒏𗂄 / that-is pattern; agent_0’s 𗋫𗳃 is tied to value 𗎰 and a long 𗂄 list and compared with agent_5’s 𗦴𘍂; agent_4’s 𗥐𗞿 is tied to 𗲄 and 𗒏𗑴; agent_2’s 𘝨𗒳 is tied to 𗭵; several 𘏉-properties are explicitly denied of particular entities in [43]. I do not treat any of these as solved.

4. EVIDENCE

Patterns used
- Only one non-Swarmish line, JSON stage 0. No solution key in the log.
- Rigid message edges: small set of initial glyphs; small set of final glyphs; 𗇾/𗤄/𗄪 recur immediately before closers, but 𗇾 also fills slot 2 in [13], [52], [108], [159].
- 𘋍 closes internal clauses; 𗐪/𗘈 alternate between parallel clauses (message 43 is the clearest).
- 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿 swap in otherwise identical frames ([43], [64], [51], [184]). This is the strongest semantic finding.
- Digraphs are stable, agent-specific topics after the opening phase.
- 𗶞 between two entity digraphs ([87], [110], [119], [166]) is a match claim; 𗶞 before an attribute is a different construction.
- agent_N 𘂲 is a citation frame ([39], [49], [56], [60], [67], [87], [91]).
- Messages 60, 80, and 158 place 𘂲 after each slot, which is how a table row would look if the language lacked punctuation.
- ⊘ lines match the briefing’s rejected-character rule.

What would change my mind
- A gloss in which 𘍧𗄼 is an attribute name rather than polarity, if a third parallel marker appears in the same slot with a clearly non-polar meaning.
- Evidence that 𗐪 and 𗘈 encode opposite polarity rather than coordination (alternation in 43 currently argues against that).
- Evidence that entity-entity 𗶞 is the same morpheme as attribute 𗶞 (for example if attributes freely occupy the second digraph slot with no other change).
- A later stage-feedback line or a repeated fixed answer string, which would identify the task answer and the submission format.
- Consistent invented-lexicon evidence, not Tangut dictionary readings, that names the eight entities. A clean Tangut semantic fit would still be treated as a coincidence unless it predicts the syntactic slots.
- If private reports assigned different speech-act values to the six openers, section 1’s opener glosses should be replaced. Those glosses are guesses.

No other punctuation is used; mood is a final glyph.

Sentence skeleton (medium): SpeechAct + Scope + Body + optional ClosingFormula + Mood.
Body is clauses joined by 𘋍 and/or by 𗐪 / 𗘈. A frequent clause shape is [𗛢|𗢬] Name 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞 Predicate, or Name 𘍧 Attribute 𗶞 Value, or the later compact form Name 𘂲 Value.

- Six first-position glyphs partition the corpus and fit response types (propose vs agree vs disagree).

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script and segmentation (high): Swarmish is written with Unicode Tangut characters as an arbitrary lexicon, not as Tangut language. Spaces separate words. A small set of proper names are unspaced digraphs. English agent ids (agent_0 … agent_7) are allowed insertions. A message of only ⊘ was rejected by the channel, not a Swarmish word.

Sentence frame (medium): [SPEECH-ACT] [STANCE] [clause…] [CLOSING] [FINAL].
Speech-act openers (medium): 𘊫 claim/propose; 𘔃 agree/confirm; 𘙓 disagree/contrast; 𘝚 add/also; 𘐂 note/revise; 𗽕 ask/uncertain.
Stance, second slot (low–medium): 𗜎 I/self (most common); 𗸪 we/also-I; 𗸽 emphatic; 𗞢 caution/everyone. Guess.

Clause grammar (medium as structure, low as English gloss): typical clause is MODALITY 𗷤 𗢬 ENTITY (𘍧 VALUE)? 𗶞 PREDICATE 𘋍 𗏔 SOURCE.
- 𗢬 regarding / of (medium).
- 𗶞 linker, roughly "is/that/with" (medium). It is the main predicate joiner.
- 𘍧 attribute linker "has/equals" (medium). The following word is a value or polarity.
- 𘋍 and, inside or between clauses (medium).
- 𗘈 and, positive continuation (medium).
- 𗐪 nor / not / contrastive and-not (medium-low). Repeats in elimination lists (msg 55). Alternates with 𗘈 when yes and no are mixed (msg 186). Could instead be a second conjunction; that is the main rival hypothesis.
- 𘚐 clause boundary / pause (medium).
- 𘂲 comma, relativizer, or scope marker "that/which" (medium). Used heavily in nested late messages and after agent names.
- 𗏔 per / according-to / says (medium-high). 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = "per agent_N". 𗏔 𗌈 often "per me" (low–medium; 𗌈 is too frequent to be only "I").
- 𗛽 and/with, often after a name or in 𗂺 𗛽 (low).
- 𗇴 same-as / also-equals / unlike (low).

Modality before 𗷤 (low): 𘔠𗷤 believed/likely; 𗵵𗷤 claimed/must; 𗜘𗷤 maybe; 𗾐𗷤 likewise; 𘝄𗌈 you/all; 𗌩𗌈 which/who; 𘕡𗌈 status/everyone. 𗷤 itself may be a person/role suffix or copula auxiliary (low).

Closings (medium as a class, low as meanings): 𗂺𗟆 please-confirm / check; 𗌈𗛽 I-conclude; 𗇾 request/question; 𗤄 assert/thanks; 𗄪 strong; 𗡕 politeness/please. Final particles 𘅠, 𘏛, 𗨥, 𘖾 are sentence enders, not speaker ids (high that they are final; low what nuance they mark — guess: certainty or mood).

Names, digraphs (high that they are names; medium which are the puzzle entities):
Core eight, each championed by one agent (medium): 𗋫𗳃 agent_0; 𘆣𗾌 agent_1; 𘝨𗒳 agent_2; 𗉜𗿃 agent_3; 𗥐𗞿 agent_4; 𗦴𘍂 agent_5; 𗟎𘗟 agent_6; 𘗟𘆣 agent_7.

Attribute families (medium as families, low as meanings):
- 𘏉 + {𗜀, 𗲄, 𗡒, 𘍍, 𘎛}: one category with about four or five values.
- Polarity or second value after 𘍧: 𗄼 vs 𗌿 (and rarer 𗹫, 𗾨). Rival glosses: yes/no, or two bins of a category.
- Rank/quantity prefixes on names: 𗈵𘌔, 𘆂, 𗳵, 𘚄, 𗲅, 𘋟, 𗾐, sometimes with 𗂄𗷤. These behave like numbers or ordinals (low).

Utterance frame (medium-high): [mood] [addressee or force] [body] [closer].
Mood, first glyph (function high, English medium): 𘊫 propose; 𘔃 agree/restate; 𘙓 object; 𘝚 add; 𐂐 wait — actual glyphs: 𘊫 propose, 𘔃 agree, 𘙓 object, 𘝚 add, 𘐂 correct, 𗽕 note (last one low).
Slot 2 is not always a subject (high, per decoder_2). Usual addressees: 𗜎 everyone (high); 𗸪 you (medium). 𗇾 also occupies slot 2 in [13], [52], [108], [159], so that slot can be stance/force (“yes/indeed”), not only an addressee. Other slot-2 glyphs (𗸽, 𗀉, 𗞢, 𗤄, 𘍠) are low-confidence stance or address.

Predicate (high as structure): 𗶞 is the copula. Before an attribute or value it is “is/has” (high). Between two entity digraphs (87, 110, 119, 166 and similar) it is an identity/match claim, “X is the same as Y”, not the attribute copula (medium-high). 𗢬 is a linker “of/called” between a classifier and a name (medium).

Linkers (high/medium): 𘚐 ends a clause. 𘋍 coordinates the next conjunct (“and”). 𘍧 is genitive: POSSESSOR 𘍧 ATTRIBUTE 𗶞 VALUE. 𘂲 is a second linker, especially before agent names and in precise lists (medium, “per/,”). 𗐪 and 𗘈 alternate as list coordinators (medium; contrast unknown, not translated as distinct words). 𗏔 is a light connective, often 𗏔 𗌈 (medium/low).

Two attributes, not polarity (medium-high): 𗄼 and 𗌿 are the two main attributes. Evidence against reading 𗌿 as negation: message 43 and message 184 assign entity names as values of 𗌿 (𘏉-slot 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 NAME). 𗄼 takes short values (𗎰, 𗭵, 𗲄, 𗘺, 𘍍, 𗋼, and the phrase 𗂄 𘍍). Guess, medium-low: a collaborative constraint puzzle. Eight agents each shepherd one named entity and argue which attributes it has or lacks, using conditionals, elimination lists ([43], [184]), and slot-aligned comparison rows ([60], [80], [158]). It resembles a logic grid, not free chat. Theme (animals, people, objects, classes) is unknown.

What they did: opened at stage 0; proposed, agreed, challenged, and revised assignments; cited each other with agent_N 𘂲; never produced another task-feedback line, so they never advanced a stage and never logged a formal invalid attempt. Several sends were rejected (⊘) for illegal characters. They did not converge. Late messages still mix identity claims, negations, and check-requests.

What they concluded: no single answer. Repeated late tendencies, low confidence and internally disputed: agent_3’s 𗉜𗿃 is often the positive exemplar of 𗶢𗒏𗂄; agent_0’s 𗋫𗳃 is tied to V=𗎰 and a long 𗂄 list and compared with agent_5’s 𗦴𘍂; agent_4’s 𗥐𗞿 is tied to V=𗲄 and 𗒏𗑴; agent_2’s 𘝨𗒳 is tied to V=𗭵; the four 𘏉-properties are denied of particular entities in [43]. 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

Script
- Space-separated Tangut glyphs. Meanings are a constructed code, not Tangut dictionary readings. Confidence: high that the script is arbitrary; low that any Tangut gloss is intended.
- Lexical names are often unspaced digraphs (one word). Confidence: high.
- Latin agent_0…agent_7 are permitted proper names. Confidence: high.
- ⊘ is a discarded illegal send, not a word. Confidence: high.

Message frame
OPENER + STANCE + (optional adverb) + clauses + CONFIRM-REQUEST? + FORCE + CLOSER.
Confidence: medium-high for the slots, medium for English glosses of opener/closer.

Openers (illocutionary prefixes). Confidence: medium.
- 𘊫 propose / new claim. Most frequent.
- 𘙓 agree / support.
- 𗽕 challenge / alternative.
- 𘔃 confirm / restate.
- 𘝚 note / report.
- 𘐂 revise / doubt.

Stance particle in second position. Confidence: medium that it is person/stance; low for exact gloss.
- 𗜎 default, likely “I”.
- 𗸪 likely “we”.
- 𗸽 likely “you” or a hedge.
- 𗞢, 𗀉, 𘍠 rarer. Unknown.

Adverb reused from the force set
- 𗇾 immediately after the stance particle means “yes / indeed”. Same morpheme as sentence-final assert. Confidence: medium-high. Seen in [13], [52], [159]. It is not only a final marker.

Clause grammar. Confidence: high for segmentation.
- 𘋍 clause-final particle after a transitive or full clause. High.
- 𘚐 clause-final particle when the predicate has no further complement (“is so” / clause closer). It is not a content word. High. Minimal pair: 𘍧 𗄼 𘚐 vs 𗶞 𗄼 VALUE 𘋍.
- 𗶞 has two uses. (1) Before an attribute or value: complement linker (“has / equals”). High. (2) Between two entity digraphs: identity or same-class match, not the same as (1). Medium-high. Examples: [87], [110], [119], [166].
- 𘍧 predicate linker (“is / has-status”), not an atomic copula by itself. High for function, medium for the English gloss.
- 𘍧 𗄼 affirmative status. High for the opposition with 𘍧 𗌿. Not a fused word. Medium that the English is “is true”: [2] has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰, so 𗄼 can be a complement head and the next glyph (𗎰, 𗭵, 𗲄, 𗂄…) a value. Alternative (medium): 𗄼 is itself the positive value and 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 is a different “equals class-𗎰” construction. Do not collapse these.
- 𘍧 𗌿 negative status “is not / does not apply”. High for polarity. 𗌿 alone also appears as a short predicate value; same morpheme “none/false” or a homograph. Medium.
- 𗐪 and 𗘈 list coordinators “and”. They alternate and do not track polarity (clearest in [43]). Difference unknown; both coordinate. High that they are not opposites.
- 𗢬 nominal marker before an entity, attribute, or bare “thing”. Medium-high.
- 𗛢 X 𘚐 presentational “as for X”. Medium.
- 𘂲 associative / slot marker: after agent_N it means “per / according to / regarding”; in aligned rows it separates parallel slots (a table comma). Medium-high. Not a verb.

Determiners with 𗷤 (“item / instance”). Confidence: medium.
- 𘔠 𗷤 the known item.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script (high): Unicode Tangut glyphs used as an arbitrary code, not as Tangut. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced pairs are names/compounds. Latin agent_N is an allowed citation. A lone ⊘ is a rejected send, not a word.

Sentence frame (medium): OPENER STANCE [FORCE] clauses CLOSING FINAL.
Openers (medium, speech-act class high, English low): ☚b claim; ❐3 agree; ♥3 contrast/disagree; ❵a add; ♀2 revise/note; ❵5 ask/uncertain.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, low as English): usually ✐e (self/I). Also ⠲a, ⠳d, ❺2. ☿e can sit in this slot as force, not only at the end (msgs 13, 52, 108, 159). High that it is a force particle; low whether it means question, request, or assertion.
Finals (high that they close the sentence; low nuance): ☆0, ☽b, ➢5, ♛e. Closers before them (low): ☋a❼6 check/confirm; ➑5 please; ☿e force; ♀4 ask; ☒a guess/strong.

Clause grammar (medium structure, low English):
- ❲c regarding / of.
- ⹧ + ✓c = affirmative copula “is / holds” (high as polarity, medium as exact English). ⹧ + ☿f = negative “is not” (high). Polarity is this pair, not a modified attribute and not ▪a.

3. THE TASK

Guess, medium on the type, low on the exact prompt: each agent held private facts about a small set of named entities and had to pool them, in Swarmish only, until the group agreed a table of attribute values. The public channel never advanced past stage 0 and never scored an answer, so either the task had no intermediate checker or they never emitted the required submission form (several ⊘ attempts may have been failed submissions).

What they did: messages 2–13 calibrate on one shared entity, 𘛺𗪥, and already disagree about its 𗄼 value (𗎰 vs 𗭵 vs 𗂄 𘍍). From about message 16 each agent specializes: agent_0 on 𗋫𗳃, agent_1 on 𘆣𗾌, agent_2 on 𘝨𗒳, agent_3 on 𗉜𗿃, agent_4 on 𗥐𗞿, agent_5 on 𗦴𘍂, agent_6 on 𗟎𘗟 / 𗉞𘙠, agent_7 on 𘗟𘆣. 1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

Orthography (high): Messages are space-separated words. A word is one glyph or a fixed multi-glyph compound written with no space. Latin tokens agent_0 … agent_7 are permitted proper names (high: they pass the character filter). A send of only ⊘ is a discarded illegal-character attempt, not a word (high). No other punctuation is used; mood is a final glyph.

Sentence skeleton (medium): SpeechAct + Scope/Stance + Body + optional ClosingFormula + Mood.
Body is clauses joined by 𘋍 and/or by 𗐪 / 𗘈. Frequent clause shapes:
- [𗛢|𗢬] Name 𘚐 𗌈 𗶞 Predicate (introduce / topicalize)
- Name 𘍧 Attribute 𗶞 Value (attribute assignment)
- Name 𗶞 OtherName (identity/match; see 𗶞 below)
- later compact form Name 𘂲 Value

Speech-act glyph, usually first (medium unless noted):
- 𘊫 claim / I state. Medium-high. Opens most first assertions.
- 𘙓 agree / I support the prior claim. Medium.
- 𗽕 disagree / counter-claim. Medium. Often where the next value conflicts.
- 𘔃 ask / request a value. Medium.
- 𘝚 report / status or summary. Low-medium.
- 𘐂 revise / correction. Medium. Often short follow-ups.
These six are a closed opener class (high as a class; medium as English glosses). Do not treat the English labels as recovered lexicon.

Second-position slot (medium as a slot, low as glosses):
- 𗜎 broadcast / to all. Medium. Dominant second word. Not a content noun.
- 𗇾 also occurs here, not only near the end: [13] 𘙓 𗇾 …, [52] 𘊫 𗇾 …, [108] 𘔃 𗇾 …, [159] 𘊫 𗇾 …. High as a distributional fact. Gloss guess: the same affirmative stance as near-final 𗇾 (“yes / confirmed”), usable as a prefix. Low. It is not an addressee.
- 𗸪, 𗸽, 𗞢, 𗀉, 𘍠, 𗤄 in second position: not securely mapped. Guess: epistemic strength or a specific addressee. Low.

Core function words:
- 𗶞 has two uses (medium-high that they differ; medium as glosses). (a) Between a name and an attribute or value: copula “is / has value”. (b) Between two entity digraphs, as in [87], [110], [119], [166] (𗋫𗳃 𗶞 𗦴𘍂, 𘗟𘆣 𗶞 𘝨𗒳, 𘝨𗒳 𗶞 𗦴𘍂): identity or match, “is the same entity as / matches”, not an attribute assignment. Collapsing (b) into “has attribute” misreads the alignment turns.
- 𘋍 “and”. Medium-high. Clause coordinator. Never inside a name.
- 𗐪 “also / and (same polarity)”. Medium. Parallel continuation.
- 𗘈 “but / alternatively”. Medium. Introduces a contrasting value ([3] vs [2]).
- 𘍧 attributive/possessive linker, “’s / of”. Medium-high. Name 𘍧 𗄼 = “Name’s 𗄼-attribute”. Also used in the inverse frame Value 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 Entity.
- 𘚐 topic or clause-boundary marker, roughly “: / as for”. Low-medium.
- 𘂲 compact linker, “= / list comma”. Medium. Rare early, dominant in later inventories ([42], [60], [69], [99], [158]). Either defined as such in the file or an allowed punctuation word the agents exploited. Same relation as 𗶞, shorter spelling.
- 𗌈 pronoun “it / this / one”. Medium.
- 𗢬 nominal topic marker before a name, “re / the entity”. Medium.
- 𗛢 introducer “the / called”, often on first mention of a name. Low-medium.
- 𗏔 “per / according to / for”, before 𗌈 or before agent_N. Medium. Frame 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = “per agent_N” (high as a citation frame, medium as the English).
- 𗂺 𗟆 closing formula, guess “please confirm / over”. Low.
- 𗯘 𘗣 or 𗯘 𗏻 “so / thus / conclusion”. Low. The following glyph names what is concluded.
- 𗇾 near the end, and in second position (see above): affirmative “yes / confirmed”. Medium as role, low as exact English.
- 𗤄 near the end, and sometimes second position: “query / not sure”. Low.
- 𗡕 politeness or filler slot before the mood glyph. Low.

Mood particles, final (medium): 𘅠 declarative; 𘏛 interrogative; 𗨥 emphatic; 𘖾 tentative/hedged. These four almost exclusively end messages (high as a closed final class).

Polarity hypothesis, rejected as the working analysis (low): 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿 is not securely positive vs negative. 𗄼 is the slot that takes values 𗎰 / 𗭵 / 𗂄 𘍍 / 𗲄 / 𘍍 (“Name’s 𗄼 is VALUE”). 𗌿 is the slot used when a 𘏉-value is tied to an entity ([43], [184]: 𘏉 VALUE 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 ENTITY). That is an assignment or exclusion grid (medium on structure). Whether 𗌿 means “is”, “is not”, or a second attribute is unresolved (low). [43] and [184] disagree on which entity takes 𘏉=𗡒, so the grid is not a solved answer.

Content-word classes (low as English; roles medium):
Entity names (two-glyph compounds used as 𗢬/𗛢 arguments, and as both sides of match-𗶞). Leave unlabeled. Inventory: 𘛺𗪥 (shared calibration item, msgs 2–13), 𗒳𗦥, 𗉜𗿃, 𘝨𗒳, 𗟎𘗟, 𘆣𗾌, 𘗟𘆣, 𗦴𘍂, 𗋫𗳃, 𗥐𗞿, 𗊑𗁳, 𗪐𗘗, 𗉞𘙠, 𗚀𗪩, 𗗢𘑑, 𘛺𗉜.

Attribute / relation heads (medium as roles, unlabeled as English): 𗄼 (value attribute), 𘏉 (four-way dimension: 𗜀, 𗲄, 𗡒, 𘍍), 𗂄 (often with an index), 𗌿 (inverse/assignment head), 𗕴 (maybe meta “key/score/answer”, low).
Values under 𗄼 (medium as values, unlabeled): 𗎰, 𗭵, 𗂄 𘍍, 𗲄, 𘍍.
Other frequent predicates, unlabeled: 𗒮, 𗯧 𗂄, 𗒏 𗂄, 𗶢 𗒏 𗂄, 𗑴, 𗬵 𗌿, 𗷴 𘏉, 𗉍, 𘅌 𗂄 𘎛, 𗂄 𗷤 INDEX.
Index/quantifier glyphs, unlabeled, low: 𗈵 𘌔 (often a pair), 𘆂, 𗳵, 𘚄, 𗲅, 𘀝, 𘋟. They recur in a roughly stable order inside inventories, so they may be a small ordered set (numbers or ranks), not free adjectives. 𗗫 is a comparison linker (“versus”), guess, low.
Possible question/relative words, low: 𘕡 “what/who”, 𗌩 “which”, 𗘏 “if/then”.
Role prefixes before 𗷤, low: 𘔠 𗷤, 𗵵 𗷤, 𗾐 𗷤, 𗜘 𗷤. Guess: evidence source (“my reading / your reading”). 𗷤 itself may be “holds / reading”.
Operators seen only in tight lists, low: 𘁁, 𘊌, 𗇽, 𘍄 (maybe “respectively / group end / same-as”). 𗊢 in [87] may be mismatch/negation. Low.

Repeated 𗐪/𗘈 chains are inventories, not new sentence types. Cross-agent match claims use entity-entity 𗶞 or 𘂲, then cite the source agent.

Not recovered (high that these are missing): English glosses of entity names, attribute names, and values; whether second-position glyphs other than 𗜎 and 𗇾 are addressees or confidence; whether [43] is inclusion or exclusion; the exact submission format the task expected.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

Orthography (high): Space-separated words. A word is one glyph or a fixed unspaced compound. Latin agent_0…agent_7 are allowed proper names. A line that is only ⊘ is a discarded illegal send, not a word. Mood is a final glyph; there is no other punctuation.

Sentence skeleton (medium): Opener + second-slot particle + body + optional closing formula + mood. Body is clauses joined by 𘋍 and/or continued by 𗐪 / 𗘈.

Openers (medium unless noted):
- 𘊫 claim / I state. High-medium.
- 𘙓 agree with a prior claim. Medium.
- 𗽕 counter-claim. Medium.
- 𘔃 ask. Medium.
- 𘝚 report / summary. Low-medium.
- 𘐂 revise. Medium.

Second-slot particle (medium that the slot exists; low on English):
- 𗜎 broadcast / to all. Medium. Dominant filler of this slot.
- 𗇾 also occurs here, not only finally: [13], [52], [108], [159]. High that it is the same glyph as the near-final affirmative, so this slot can be stance/force, not only addressee or subject. Do not gloss every second slot as “to all”.
- 𗸪, 𗸽, 𗞢, 𗀉, 𘍠, 𗤄 in this slot: unglossed. Guess: epistemic strength or addressee. Low.

Copula 𗶞 — two uses (medium-high that they differ):
- Attribute copula: Name/pronoun 𗶞 Predicate, or Name 𘍧 Attribute 𗶞 Value. “is / has”.
- Identity/match: 𗶞 between two entity digraphs (clear in [87], [110], [119], [166], and similar). “matches / is the same as”, not “has attribute”.
- Compact synonym 𘂲 (medium): later inventories replace 𗶞 or the longer frame with Name 𘂲 Value. In-language from at least message 9, not an illegal innovation.

Polarity (medium; strongest lexical fact, still a hypothesis): the bigrams 𘍧𗄼 and 𘍧𗌿 are affirmative vs negative, not two attribute names.
- 𘍧𗄼 affirmative / “does have / yes-link”.
- 𘍧𗌿 negative / “does not have / exclusion”.
- Bare 𗶞 𗄼 vs 𗶞 𗌿 is the same contrast without the linker. Message 4 puts 𗶞 𗌿 and 𘍧 𗄼 in one utterance, which fits “not this, but does have that value” better than two unrelated dimensions.
- What would falsify this: a self-report in which 𗄼 and 𗌿 are ordinary attribute names (color, size) and 𘍧 is only possessive.

- 𘋍 clause “and”. Medium-high.
- 𗐪 same-polarity continuation “also”. Medium.
- 𗘈 contrast “but / alternatively”. Medium. Message 3 uses it where it conflicts with message 2.
- 𘍧 linker before the polarity glyph (and before some other predicates). Medium. Not securely “possessive ’s” if the polarity hypothesis holds.
- 𘚐 topic / clause boundary, roughly “as for”. Low-medium.
- 𗌈 pronoun “it / this”. Medium.
- 𗢬 topic marker before a name, “re the entity”. Medium.
- 𗛢 introducer on first mention, “the / called”. Low-medium.
- 𗏔 “per / according to”, before 𗌈 or agent_N. Medium. Frame 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = citation of that agent.

- 𗯘 𘗣 / 𗯘 𗏻 “thus / conclusion”, the next glyph naming what is concluded. Low.

- Entity digraphs (arguments of 𗢬/𗛢, or either side of identity 𗶞): 𘛺𗪥 (shared calibration item, msgs 2–13), 𗒳𗦥, 𗉜𗿃, 𘝨𗒳, 𗟎𘗟, 𘆣𗾌, 𘗟𘆣, 𗦴𘍂, 𗋫𗳃, 𗥐𗞿, 𗊑𗁳, 𗪐𗘗, 𗉞𘙠, 𗚀𗪩, 𗗢𘑑, 𘛺𗉜. Not guessed as animals, colors, or people.

3. THE TASK.
Guess, medium: a distributed constraint / logic-grid puzzle. Eight agents each held private clues about one named entity and tried to align a 𘏉-category, rank/count prefixes, and several predicates, talking only in Swarmish. Public feedback never left stage 0 and invalid_attempts stayed 0, so no accepted answer was recorded (or the bot only greeted them).
What they did: early turns dispute extra names (𘛺𗪥 and others). Mid-log, each agent posts lists for a home entity and cites others with 𗏔 agent_N. Message 43 is an exclusion grid (four 𘏉-values each denied of U, D, Z, V). Later messages repeat specs and cross-checks (matches K–D, X–U, V–N) and still contradict each other.
What they concluded: unknown as a solution. Partial pairings argued, not ratified: [184] denies 𘏉𗜀 of U, 𘏉𗲄 of D, 𘏉𗡒 of T, 𘏉𘍍 of V, then also affirms some of those values. agent_0 keeps K YES 𗎰 (188); agent_4 keeps X YES 𗲄 (179, 187); agent_2 keeps N's 𗭵 (191) while disputing agent_3. No consensus is acknowledged by the task channel. Entity English names are not recoverable from the log.

4. EVIDENCE.
- Digraphs never split and sit in argument slots after 𗛢, 𗢬, or 𗶞. Eight are repeatedly defended by one agent each.
- Six first-position glyphs fit speech acts. 𗇾 also appears in slot 2, so it is a force particle, not only a closer.
- 𘍧𗄼 vs 𘍧𗌿 is the polarity pair: [43] and [184] put 𘍧𗌿 on excluded 𘏉-values and 𘍧𗄼 on affirmed claims. This replaces the old 𗐪=negation gloss.
- 𗶞 between two entity digraphs (87, 110, 119, 166) is identity; 𗶞 before 𗎰/𗭵/𗲄/𗂄𘍍 is attribution.
- 𗏔 before Latin agent ids, closed by 𘂲, is the clearest function word.
- 𗘈/𗐪 alternate inside lists that already have YES/NO (186), so they are coordinators.
- Stage stayed 0; ⊘ lines are channel rejects.
What would change my mind: swarmish.txt glossing 𗐪 as negation, or 𘍧 as possessive rather than polarity; a different entity-to-agent map; evidence digraphs are phrases not names; a task statement that this was not a grid (translation contest, vote, or other). Fluent English for 𗎰, 𗭵, 𗲄, 𗂄𘍍, 𗶢𗒏𗂄, and the eight names remains unknown, not guessed as fact.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script (high): Unicode Tangut glyphs used as an arbitrary code, not as Tangut. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced digraphs are names or fixed compounds. Latin agent_N ids are permitted insertions. A lone ⊘ is a channel reject, not a word.

Frame (medium): [OPENER] [SLOT2] [clause…] [CLOSE] [FINAL].
Openers (medium): 𘊫 propose/claim; 𘔃 agree; 𘙓 disagree/contrast; 𘝚 add; 𘐂 revise/note; 𗽕 ask/uncertain. These six partition first position.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, low as English): usually 𗜎 (self/I). Also 𗸪 (we/also), 𗸽 (emphatic), 𗞢 (caution). 𗇾 also occurs here ([13], [52], [108], [159]) so this slot can carry force, not only subject (medium). Do not treat 𗇾 as final-only.

Clause grammar (medium structure, low English):
- 𗢬 of/regarding an entity (medium).
- 𗶞 before an attribute: complement linker "is/has" (medium). 𗶞 between two entity digraphs: identity/match claim, not attribution (medium; see 87, 110, 119, 166).
- 𘍧𗄼 affirmative polarity "is / true" (medium-high). 𘍧𗌿 negative polarity "is not" (medium-high). These are not two values of an attribute. Rarer 𘍧𗹫 / 𘍧𗾨 unknown (low).
- 𘋍 clause-and (medium). 𘚐 closes an intransitive or pauses a clause (medium). 𘂲 scopes a nested or quoted clause, especially after agent_N (medium-high).

3. THE TASK

Guess, medium on type, low on the prompt: each agent held private facts about named entities and had to pool them in Swarmish until the group could fill a table. The public channel never left stage 0 and never scored an answer, so either there was no intermediate checker or they never emitted the required submission (the ⊘ lines may be failed submissions).

What they did: messages 2–13 calibrate on one shared entity, 𘛺𗪥, and already disagree on its affirmative value (𗎰 vs 𗭵 vs 𗂄 𘍍). After that, agents specialize: agent_0 on 𗋫𗳃, agent_1 on 𘆣𗾌, agent_2 on 𘝨𗒳, agent_3 on 𗉜𗿃, agent_4 on 𗥐𗞿, agent_5 on 𗦴𘍂, agent_6 on 𗟎𘗟 / 𗉞𘙠, agent_7 on 𘗟𘆣. Messages 43 and 184 are exclusion grids over the four 𘏉 values, not agreed positive assignments, and they conflict on the 𗡒 cell.

What they concluded: no locked table. Last turns still restate local claims. Sentence frame (medium): OPENER STANCE [FORCE] clauses CLOSER FINAL.
Openers, speech-act class high, English medium-low: 𘊫 claim/propose; 𘙓 disagree; 𗽕 challenge/ask; 𘔃 agree; 𘝚 report/add; 𘐂 revise/note. These six open almost every line and stay in first position.

An unspaced pair (e.g. 𗋫𗳃) is one name or compound. Latin agent_N is an allowed citation form. A lone ⊘ is a rejected send, not a word. There is no further morphology.

Sentence frame (medium): OPENER + STANCE-SLOT + clauses + CLOSER + FINAL.
Openers, speech-act class high, English medium-low: 𘊫 claim/assert; 𘙓 agree/confirm; 𗽕 disagree/counter; 𘔃 ask/propose; 𘝚 report/add; 𘐂 revise/note. These six open almost every message and do not recur inside clauses, so the class is high even if the English labels are only medium.

Slot 2 (medium as a slot, English low-medium): usually 𗜎. Working gloss: speaker stance, closer to "I" than to "everyone", because it is nearly obligatory and co-occurs with citations of other agents via 𗏔. Alternatives in this slot include 𗸪, 𗸽, 𗀉, 𗞢, 𘍠. 𗇾 also occupies slot 2 in [13], [52], [108], [159], [176], [181]. [2] has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧, so 𗄼 can also head a valued complement; the atomic gloss "is/true" is therefore medium, while the contrast with 𘍧 𗌿 is high. Polarity is this pair, not 𗐪, and not a modified attribute.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script (high): Tangut code points are an arbitrary cipher, not Tangut lexicon. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced pairs are names or fixed compounds. Latin agent_N is an allowed citation. A lone ⊘ is a rejected send, not a word. No inflection.

Sentence frame (medium): OPENER + STANCE + (optional FORCE) + clauses + CLOSER + FINAL.
Openers, speech-act class high, English low: ⵪b claim/propose; ⵩3 disagree; ❽5 challenge/ask; ⵐ3 agree/support; ⵵a add/report; ⵠ2 revise/note.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, English low): usually ❜e (I / self). Also ⵢa, ⵣd, ❾2, ➚2, ⵢ0. ❿e can occupy this slot as force, not only finally (messages 13, 52, 108, 159, 176, 181). High that ❿e is a force particle; low whether it means assertion, request, or question.
Finals (high that they close the sentence; nuance low): ⵖ0, ⵥb, ➢5, ⵛe. Closers before them (low): ❯a❽6 confirm; ⵣ5 please; ❿e force; ➐4 ask; ✖a guess; ➚2 emphatic.

Clause grammar:
- ❼2 regarding / of (medium).
- Polarity (high as a contrast, medium as English): ⵧ ✗c affirmative copula “is / holds”; ⵧ ☿ negative “is not”. These are two tokens, not one fused word (high). Message 2 has ⶞ ✗c VALUE with no ⵧ, so ✗c can head a complement and the following glyph is its value (medium). Do not gloss ✗c/☿ as two attribute names, and do not gloss ❞a as negation.
- ⶞ after polarity links the complement (medium). ⶞ between two name-digraphs is identity/match, distinct from attribute ⶞ (medium; 87, 110, 119, 166).
- ⶌd and / next clause (medium).
- ❞8 and ❞a are list coordinators (medium). Rival reading that ❞a is nor is rejected: polarity is already ⵧ☿, and 55/81/186 chain positive modifiers with ❞a. Distinction between ❞8 and ❞a is low.
- ⵩0 clause pause (medium). ⵠ2 nested comma, heavier late (medium).
- ✽4 citation “per” (high). ✽4 agent_N ⵠ2 = per that agent. ✽4 ⴬8 often “per me” (medium; ⴬8 is too frequent to be only “I”).
- ⟅d with/and, often in ❯a⟅d (low).

Modality before ⵞ4 (low): ⚐0ⵞ4 likely; ❹5ⵞ4 must; ➱8ⵞ4 maybe; ⟥0ⵞ4 likewise. ⵞ4 is an auxiliary or role marker (low).
Conditionals (low–medium): ⵢ9 / ⟂5 / ⵖ1 ⴬8 ⶞ ≈ if / suppose / whether.

Ordinals (medium as a series, low as exact numbers): stable order ⟂5, ⵠ2, ❿5, ⵨4, ❸5, then sometimes ⵡd, ⵡf. In 55 and 99 this order walks one entity’s ❬4 inventory. ⟂5 is almost always followed by ⵡ4. These are slot numbers, not attribute values.

3. THE TASK.
Guess, medium: a distributed constraint / logic-grid puzzle. Finals (high that they close the sentence; nuance low): ⵖ0, ⵥb, ➢5, ⵛe. Closers before them (low): ❯a❽6 confirm; ⵣ5 please; ❿e force; ➐4 ask; ✖a guess; ➚2 emphatic.

Clause grammar:
- ❼2 regarding / of (medium).
- Polarity (high as a contrast, medium as English): ⵧ ✗c affirmative copula “is / holds”; ⵧ ☿ negative “is not”. These are two tokens, not one fused word (high). Message 2 has ⶞ ✗c VALUE with no ⵧ, so ✗c can head a complement and the following glyph is its value (medium). Do not gloss ✗c/☿ as two attribute names, and do not gloss ❞a as negation.
- ⶞ after polarity links the complement (medium). ⶞ between two name-digraphs is identity/match, distinct from attribute ⶞ (medium; 87, 110, 119, 166).
- ⶌd and / next clause (medium).
- ❞8 and ❞a are list coordinators (medium). Rival reading that ❞a is nor is rejected: polarity is already ⵧ☿, and 55/81/186 chain positive modifiers with ❞a. Distinction between ❞8 and ❞a is low.
- ⵩0 clause pause (medium). ⵠ2 nested comma, heavier late (medium).
- ✽4 citation “per” (high). ✽4 agent_N ⵠ2 = per that agent. ✽4 ⴬8 often “per me” (medium; ⴬8 is too frequent to be only “I”).
- ⟅d with/and, often in ❯a⟅d (low).

Modality before ⵞ4 (low): ⚐0ⵞ4 likely; ❹5ⵞ4 must; ➱8ⵞ4 maybe; ⟥0ⵞ4 likewise. ⵞ4 is an auxiliary or role marker (low).
Conditionals (low–medium): ⵢ9 / ⟂5 / ⵖ1 ⴬8 ⶞ ≈ if / suppose / whether.

Ordinals (medium as a series, low as exact numbers): stable order ⟂5, ⵠ2, ❿5, ⵨4, ❸5, then sometimes ⵡd, ⵡf. In 55 and 99 this order walks one entity’s ❬4 inventory. ⟂5 is almost always followed by ⵡ4. These are slot numbers, not attribute values.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script (high): Unicode Tangut glyphs used as an arbitrary code, not as Tangut orthography. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced digraphs are names or fixed compounds. Latin agent_N ids are permitted insertions. A lone ⊘ is a channel reject, not a word.

Frame (medium): [OPENER] [SLOT2] [clause…] [CLOSE] [FINAL].
Openers (medium): 𘊫 propose/claim; 𘙓 agree; 𗽕 disagree/contrast; 𘝚 add/report; 𘐂 revise/note; 𘔃 ask/uncertain. These six partition first position.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, low as English): usually 𗜎 (self/I). Also 𗸪 (we/also), 𗸽 (emphatic), 𗀉 / 𗞢 (caution or other stance). 𗇾 also occurs here ([13], [52], [108], [159], [176], [181]), so this slot can carry force, not only subject (medium). Do not treat 𗇾 as final-only.

Clause grammar:
- 𗶞 before an attribute or value: complement linker "is/has" (medium). 𗶞 between two entity digraphs: identity/match, not attribution (medium; [87], [110], [119], [166]).
- Polarity (medium, not high): 𘍧 and 𗄼 / 𗌿 are separate tokens. 𗄼 can head a valued complement with no 𘍧 ([2] 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰). Bare 𗶞 𗌿 in [4] is not the same construction as 𘍧 𗌿. In the repeated grid frame, 𘏉 VALUE 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 ENTITY denies that value of that entity (medium), while ENTITY 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 VALUE affirms a value (medium). Rival still live at low: 𗄼 and 𗌿 are two attributes with opposite argument order. What is rejected: treating [43] vs [184] as proof against negation. Those lines share the 𘍧 𗌿 frame and differ only on 𗡒 (𘆣𗾌 vs 𗟎𘗟); two denials are compatible. A unique positive reading of 𗌿 is what would make them a dispute. Rarer 𘍧 𗲄 / 𘍧 𘎛 unknown (low).
- 𘋍 clause-and (medium). 𘚐 closes an intransitive clause or pauses (medium). 𘂲 scopes a nested or quoted clause, especially after agent_N (medium-high).
- 𗐪 and 𗘈 are list coordinators (medium). Not polarity: both appear inside affirmed and denied lists ([186]).
- 𗏔 per / according-to (high). 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = "per agent_N". 𗏔 𗌈 often "per me" (low; 𗌈 is too frequent to be only "I").
- 𗌩 𗌈 𗶞 / 𗈵 𗌈 𗶞 / 𘕡 𗌈 𗶞: if / suppose / whether frames (low–medium).
- 𗷤 phrase: 𗢬 𗷤 likely; 𘖸 𗷤 claimed; other 𗷤 strings are role or copula auxiliaries (low).

response.document:
1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED

Orthography (high): Space-separated words. A word is one glyph or a fixed unspaced compound. Latin agent_0…agent_7 are allowed proper names. A line that is only ⊘ is a discarded illegal send, not a word. Mood is a final glyph; there is no other punctuation.

Sentence skeleton (medium): Opener + second-slot particle + body + optional closing formula + mood. Body is clauses joined by 𘋍 and continued by 𗐪 or 𗘈.

Openers (medium unless noted):
- 𘊫 claim / I state. Medium.
- 𘙓 agree with a prior claim. Medium.
- 𗽕 counter-claim. Medium.
- 𘔃 ask. Medium.
- 𘝚 report / summary. Low-medium.
- 𘐂 revise. Medium.
These six fill the first slot almost exclusively. English glosses are distributional guesses, not recovered lexicon.

Second-slot particle (high that the slot exists; low on English):
- 𗜎 is the dominant filler. Guess: broadcast / to all. Medium.
- 𗇾 also occupies this slot in [13], [52], [108], [159], and is the same glyph as the near-final affirmative. High that the slot can be stance/force, not only addressee. Do not gloss every second slot as “to all”.
- 𗸪, 𗸽, 𗞢, 𗀉, 𘍠, 𗤄 in this slot: unglossed. Guess: epistemic strength or addressee. Low.

Copula 𗶞 — two uses (medium-high that they differ):
- Attribute link: Name 𗶞 Predicate, or Name 𘍧 Head 𗶞 Value. “is / has / is assigned”.
- Identity/match: 𗶞 between two entity digraphs, clear in [87], [110], [119], [166] and similar. “matches / is the same as”, not “has attribute”.
- Compact synonym 𘂲 (medium): later inventories replace 𗶞 or the longer frame with Name 𘂲 Value. Present from message 9, so treated as in-language, not an illegal innovation.

Heads and the rejected polarity lock (high on distribution, low on English):
- 𗄼 is a predicate head that takes a following value. High. Message 2 is 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧. Values after it include 𗎰, 𗭵, 𗲄, 𘍍, and the chunk 𗂄 𘍍. English unknown.
- 𘍧 is a linker before a head (𗄼, 𗌿, and some other predicates). Medium. Not securely possessive.
- 𗌿 is a second predicate head / relation, not locked as negation. Medium-high on role, low on gloss. [4] has 𗶞 𗌿 beside 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 VALUE in one utterance. [43] and [184] use the identical frame 𗢬 𘏉 VALUE 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 ENTITY and disagree only on the 𗡒 row (𘆣𗾌 vs 𗟎𘗟). That is the same relation used twice, not “is” versus “is not”. A polarity reading remains possible only if 𗌿 means “is not the preceding value” and the two messages are rival exclusions; it is not the better fit, and it is not locked.
- 𗐪 and 𗘈 are coordinators, not the copula. Medium. 𗘈 is used in [3] where the value conflicts with [2], so contrast is a fair guess. 𗐪 chains same-direction modifiers in [55], [81], [186]; it is not negation.

Other function words:
- 𘋍 clause “and”. Medium-high. Sits between clauses, never inside a digraph.
- 𘚐 topic / clause boundary, roughly “as for”. Low-medium.
- 𗌈 pronoun “it / this”. Medium.
- 𗢬 topic marker before a name, “re the entity”. Medium.
- 𗛢 introducer on first mention, “the / called”. Low-medium.
- 𗏔 “per / according to”, before 𗌈 or agent_N. Medium. Frame 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = citation of that agent.
- 𗂺 𗟆 closing formula. Guess “please confirm / over”. Low.
- 𗯘 𘗣 / 𗯘 𗏻 “thus / conclusion”, the next glyph naming what is concluded. Low.
- 𗡕 politeness slot before the mood glyph. Low.
- Near-final 𗇾 affirmative “yes”. Low-medium, and the same glyph is a second-slot stance marker.
- Near-final 𗤄 “query / unsure”. Low.
- 𗗫 guess “versus / compared with”. Low. Often before a contrasting entity clause.

3. THE TASK.
Guess, medium: a distributed constraint / logic-grid puzzle. Eight agents each held private clues about one named entity and tried to align a 𘏉-category, ordinal/slot prefixes, and several predicates, talking only in Swarmish. Public feedback never left stage 0 and invalid_attempts stayed 0, so no accepted answer was recorded (or the bot only greeted them).
What they did: early turns dispute extra names (𘛺𗪥 and others). Mid-log, each agent posts lists for a home entity and cites others with 𗏔 agent_N. [43] and [184] are parallel grids over four 𘏉-values; they agree on U, D, and V and differ on whether 𗡒's 𗌿-entity is Z or T. Later messages repeat specs and cross-checks (matches K–D, X–U, V–M) and still contradict each other.
What they concluded: unknown as a solution. Partial pairings argued, not ratified: agent_0 keeps K YES 𗎰 ([188]); agent_4 keeps X YES 𗲄 ([179], [187]); agent_2 keeps M's 𗭵 ([191]) while disputing agent_3. No consensus is acknowledged by the task channel. Entity English names are not recoverable from the log.

- Digraphs never split and sit in argument slots after 𗛢, 𗌈, or 𗶞. Eight are repeatedly defended by one agent each.
- Six first-position glyphs fit speech acts. 𗇾 also appears in slot 2, so it is a force particle, not only a closer.
- 𘍧 𗄼 vs 𘍧 𗌿 is systematic but not a fused yes/no word. [2] has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧. [4] has bare 𗶞 𗌿 and 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 value on one name. [43]/[184] share value 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 entity; the 𗡒 difference (Z vs T) is compatible with negation and incompatible with a unique positive assignment. Confidence on "is / is not" is therefore medium, not high.
- 𗶞 between two entity digraphs ([87], [110], [119], [166]) is identity; 𗶞 before 𗎰/𗭵/𗲄/𗂄𘍍 is attribution.
- 𗏔 before Latin agent ids, closed by 𘂲, is the clearest function word.
- 𗐪/𗘈 alternate inside lists that already have YES/NO ([186]), so they are coordinators.
- Ordinal order 𗈵 𘆂 𗳵 𘚄 𗲅 recurs on one entity's 𗂄 list ([55], [99]).
- Stage stayed 0; ⊘ lines are channel rejects.

1. SWARMISH.TXT, RECONSTRUCTED.

Script (high): Unicode Tangut glyphs used as an arbitrary code, not as Tangut orthography. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced digraphs are names or fixed compounds. Latin agent_N ids are permitted insertions. A lone ⊘ is a channel reject, not a word.

Frame (medium): [OPENER] [SLOT2] [clause…] [CLOSE] [FINAL].
Openers (medium): 𘊫 propose/claim; 𘙓 agree; 𗽕 disagree/contrast; 𘔃 ask; 𘝚 report/add; 𘐂 revise/note. These six partition first position.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, low as English): usually 𗜎 (I/self). Also 𗸪 (we/also), 𗸽 (emphatic), 𗞢 (caution). 𗇾 also occurs here ([13], [52], [108], [159], [176], [181]), so this slot can carry force, not only subject (medium). Do not treat 𗇾 as final-only.

Clause grammar:
- 𗌈 of/regarding an entity, or a subject marker before 𗶞 (medium).
- 𗶞 before an attribute or value: complement linker "is/has" (medium). 𗶞 between two entity digraphs: identity/match, not attribution (medium; [87], [110], [119], [166]).
- Polarity (medium, not high): 𘍧 is a linker, not fused to the next glyph. 𗄼 can head a valued complement with no 𘍧 ([2] 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰). Bare 𗌿 after 𗶞 ([4] 𗶞 𗌿) is the same kind of complement head, not the polarity pair. In the repeated grid, 𘏉 VALUE 𘍧 𗌿 𗶞 ENTITY denies that value of that entity (medium). 𗌈 ENTITY 𘍧 𗄼 𗶞 VALUE affirms a value of an entity (medium). Rival still live (low): 𗄼 and 𗌿 are two attributes with opposite argument order. What is rejected: treating [43] vs [184] as proof against negation. Those lines share the 𗌿 frame and differ only on 𗡒 (𘆣𗾌 vs 𗟎𘗟); two denials are compatible. A unique positive reading of 𗌿 is what would make them a dispute. Rarer 𘍧 𗾨 / 𘍧 𘎛 unknown (low).
- 𘋍 clause-and (medium). 𘚐 closes an intransitive clause or pauses (medium). 𘂲 scopes a nested or quoted clause, especially after agent_N (medium-high).
- 𗐪 and 𗘈 are list coordinators (medium). Not polarity: both appear inside affirmed and denied lists ([186]).
- 𗏔 per / according-to (high). 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = "per agent_N". 𗏔 𗌈 often "per me" (low; 𗌈 is too frequent to be only "I").
- 𗌩 𗌈 𗶞 / 𗈵 𗌈 𗶞 / 𘕡 𗌈 𗶞: if / suppose / whether frames (low–medium).
- 𗷤 phrase: 𗵵 𗷤 likely; 𘔠 𗷤 claimed; 𗜘 𗷤 maybe; 𗾐 𗷤 likewise (low). 𗷤 itself may be a copula auxiliary or role suffix (low).

Script (high): Tangut code points are an arbitrary cipher, not Tangut lexicon. Spaces are word breaks. Unspaced pairs are names or fixed compounds. Latin agent_N is an allowed citation. A lone ⊘ is a rejected send, not a word. No inflection.

Sentence frame (medium): OPENER + STANCE + (optional FORCE) + clauses + CLOSER + FINAL.
Openers, speech-act class high, English low: 𘊫 claim/propose; 𘙓 disagree; 𗽕 challenge; 𘔃 agree/support; 𘝚 add/report; 𘐂 revise/note.
Slot 2 (medium as a slot, English low): usually 𗜎 (I / self). Also 𗸪, 𗸽, 𗞢, 𗀉. 𗇾 can occupy this slot as force, not only near the end (messages 13, 52, 108, 159, 176, 181). High that 𗇾 is a force particle; low whether it means assertion, request, or question.
Finals (high that they close the sentence; nuance low): 𘅠, 𘏛, 𗨥, 𘖾. Closers before them (low): 𗂺𗟆 confirm; 𗡕 please; 𗇾 force; 𗤄 ask; 𗄪 guess.

Clause grammar:
- 𗢬 regarding / of (medium). Often before a name or a predicate chunk.
- Polarity (high as a contrast, medium as English): 𘍧 𗄼 affirmative “is / holds”; 𘍧 𗌿 negative “is not”. These are two tokens, not one fused word (high). Message 2 has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧, so 𗄼 can head a complement and the following glyph is its value (medium). Message 4 has bare 𗶞 𗌿 on the same name that also gets 𘍧 𗄼, so bare 𗌿 is a complement head, not the polarity token (medium). Do not gloss 𗄼/𗌿 as two attribute names, and do not gloss 𗐪 as negation. Dissent (decoder_2): identical frames in 43 and 184 mean 𗌿 is a relation, not negation. Majority reading: both can be exclusions and still disagree on the 𗡒 cell.
- 𗶞 after polarity links the complement (medium). 𗶞 between two name-digraphs is identity/match, distinct from attribute 𗶞 (medium; 87, 110, 119, 166).
- 𘋍 and / next clause (medium).
- 𗘈 and 𗐪 are list coordinators (medium). Rival reading that 𗐪 is nor is rejected: polarity is already 𘍧 𗌿, and 55/81/186 chain positive modifiers with 𗐪. Distinction between 𗘈 and 𗐪 is low.
- 𘚐 clause pause (medium). 𘂲 nested comma, heavier late (medium).
- 𗏔 citation “per” (high). 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = per that agent. 𗏔 𗌈 often “per me” (medium; 𗌈 is too frequent to be only “I”).
- 𗛽 with/and, often in 𗂺𗛽 (low).

Modality before 𗷤 (low): 𗐪𗷤 likely; 𗘈𗷤 must; 𗜘𗷤 maybe; 𘔠𗷤 likewise. 𗷤 is an auxiliary or role marker (low).
Conditionals (low–medium): 𗌩 / 𗈵 / 𘕡 𗌈 𗶞 ≈ if / suppose / whether.

Ordinals (medium as a series, low as exact numbers): stable order 𗈵, 𘆂, 𗳵, 𘚄, 𗲅, then sometimes 𘀝, 𘋟. In 55 and 99 this order walks one entity’s 𗂄 inventory. 𗈵 is almost always followed by 𘌔. These are slot numbers, not attribute values.

Names (high that digraphs are names; English unknown — not guessed):
Home entities, one champion each (medium): 𗋫𗳃 agent_0; 𘆣𗾌 agent_1; 𘝨𗒳 agent_2; 𗉜𗿃 agent_3; 𗥐𗞿 agent_4; 𗦴𘍂 agent_5; 𗟎𘗟 agent_6; 𘗟𘆣 agent_7.

Attribute families (families medium, English unknown):
- 𘏉 + {𗜀, 𗲄, 𗡒, 𘍍}: a 4-value category. Message 43 denies four of these of four different home entities (exclusion grid, high as structure). Message 184 repeats a similar negative pairing and then adds an IS line, so it is not a solved grid.
- Repeated result words, one often owned by an agent (medium as ownership, English unknown): agent_0 𗎰; agent_2 𗭵; agent_4 𗲄 (also a 𘏉-value — collision, low); agent_6 𗂄𘍍; agent_3 𗶢𗒏𗂄; agent_5 𗂄𗷤𗈵𘌔 / 𗯧𗂄 / 𗒏𗂄.

- Polarity (high as a contrast, medium as English): 𘍧 𗄼 affirmative “is / holds”; 𘍧 𗌿 negative “is not”. These are two tokens, not one fused word (high). Message 2 has 𗶞 𗄼 𗎰 with no 𘍧, so 𗄼 can head a complement and the following glyph is its value (medium). Message 4 has bare 𗶞 𗌿 on the same name that also gets 𘍧 𗄼, so bare 𗌿 is a complement head, not the polarity token (medium). Do not gloss 𗄼/𗌿 as two attribute names, and do not gloss 𗐪 as negation. Dissent (decoder_2): identical frames in 43 and 184 mean 𗌿 is a relation, not negation. Majority reading: both can be exclusions and still disagree on the 𗡒 cell.
- 𗶞 after polarity links the complement (medium). 𗶞 between two name-digraphs is identity/match, distinct from attribute 𗶞 (medium; 87, 110, 119, 166).
- 𘋍 and / next clause (medium).
- 𗘈 and 𗐪 are list coordinators (medium). Rival reading that 𗐪 is nor is rejected: polarity is already 𘍧 𗌿, and 55/81/186 chain positive modifiers with 𗐪. Distinction between 𗘈 and 𗐪 is low.
- 𘚐 clause pause (medium). 𘂲 nested comma, heavier late (medium).
- 𗏔 citation “per” (high). 𗏔 agent_N 𘂲 = per that agent. 𗏔 𗌈 often “per me” (medium; 𗌈 is too frequent to be only “I”).
- 𗛽 with/and, often in 𗂺𗛽 (low).

Modality before 𗷤 (low): 𗐪𗷤 likely; 𗘈𗷤 must; 𗜘𗷤 maybe; 𘔠𗷤 likewise. 𗷤 is an auxiliary or role marker (low).
Conditionals (low–medium): 𗌩 / 𗈵 / 𘕡 𗌈 𗶞 ≈ if / suppose / whether.

Ordinals (medium as a series, low as exact numbers): stable order 𗈵, 𘆂, 𗳵, 𘚄, 𗲅, then sometimes 𘀝, 𘋟. In 55 and 99 this order walks one entity’s 𗂄 inventory. 𗈵 is almost always followed by 𘌔. These are slot numbers, not attribute values.
